what.text: RU58841 is a non-steroidal antiandrogen: it blocks the androgen receptor rather than lowering hormone levels. It was developed at Roussel Uclaf in France, first reported in 1994, as a possible skin treatment for acne, male pattern hair loss and excess hair growth.

src.label: Battmann et al., J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol

what.text: In prostate cancer cells it blocked DHT's action on the androgen receptor about as strongly as hydroxyflutamide, a prostate cancer drug. The authors warned that putting it on the skin might cause body-wide effects.
No published human trials of RU58841 for hair loss found as of November 1, 2026.

research.text: Evidence for RU58841 on hair is in animals and in human scalp grafted onto mice. The search found no published or registered trial in people with hair loss. The only human study measured how the body handles one dose.
No published human studies of RU58841 for hair loss found as of November 1, 2026. A PubMed search returned 18 records, none a treatment trial in people, and ClinicalTrials.gov returned none.

research.title: How the body handles one topical dose (Okutan et al.)

facts.v: lab metabolism study, then a single-dose study in volunteers, by a sports anti-doping laboratory
one application to the scalp of a hair product with RU58841 (30 mg)
RU58841 and its breakdown products in dried blood spots and urine; the steroid profile used in doping tests

research.found: Five breakdown products were found in urine. RU58841 itself and one breakdown product were found in blood, which the authors call considerable body-wide exposure from scalp use. The steroid profile did not change. Hair was not measured.

research.title: Balding human scalp grafted onto mice (De Brouwer et al.)

facts.v: 20 scalp grafts from balding men, kept on female nude mice given testosterone
RU58841 1% in ethanol, or ethanol alone, on the grafts 5 days a week
follicles starting a new hair cycle; hair growth rate

research.found: 28% of active follicles on treated grafts started a second hair cycle vs 7% on control grafts, and hair grew faster. The authors called for a clinical trial.

src.label: De Brouwer et al., Br J Dermatol

research.text: In bald stumptailed macaques, a monkey model of male pattern baldness, RU58841 put on the scalp increased hair density, thickness and length, with no body-wide effects detected. In hamsters, it shrank androgen-dependent skin glands at very low doses applied to the skin.

src.label: Battmann et al., J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol

us.text: RU58841 is not FDA approved for any use, and no regulator approval was found anywhere. A 2026 study says it is sold by many online suppliers and marketed online for hair loss. FDA does not allow unapproved drugs to be sold for people to use, even when labelled for research. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA's drug database has no product containing RU58841. Unapproved drugs have not been reviewed by FDA for safety, effectiveness or quality.

FDA has said that companies selling unapproved drugs labelled “for research purposes” or “not for human consumption” directly to consumers for human use did so illegally. That statement was about GLP-1 drugs; FDA has not issued one naming RU58841.

items.text: the 2026 study's authors bought a 5% RU58841 hair serum over the internet and note it is available from numerous online suppliers despite having no regulatory approval.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists no trial of RU58841.

world.lead: RU58841 is not an approved medicine anywhere the search checked. No product was found in Health Canada's or EMA's records. It is not named on WADA’s list. WADA’s class for unapproved drugs (S0) may cover it, but WADA has not said so.

after.title: Sport
after.text: RU58841 is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. The lists' class S0 bans, at all times, any pharmacological substance not covered by another class that has no current approval by any government health authority for human therapeutic use, including drugs in development or discontinued. No such approval was found for RU58841, so that class’s wording may cover it. WADA has not ruled on it. A German anti-doping laboratory studied how to detect it in 2026.

side.text: There is no human safety data on RU58841 for hair loss. Studies suggest it reaches the bloodstream from the scalp, and it blocks the androgen receptor.

items.text: after one scalp application in 6 men, RU58841 and a breakdown product were found in blood.
in cells it blocked the androgen receptor about as strongly as hydroxyflutamide; the authors said skin use might cause body-wide side effects.
FDA says unapproved drugs sold 'for research purposes' (in its statement on GLP-1 drugs) are of unknown quality and may be harmful.

unconfirmed: No regulator record was found describing how RU58841 products are labelled; the 2026 study says only that it is sold by numerous online suppliers and marketed online for hair loss.
The other code names PSK-3841 and HMR-3841 come from the 2026 paper; no trial under those names was found.
UK and Australian status were not checked against a regulator record.
The 2026 study was in 6 men given one dose; long-term human exposure has not been studied.
surprises: RU58841 is discussed as a hair-loss drug, but no trial in people with hair loss was found; the only human study, from 2026, was run by an anti-doping laboratory.
It is often described as staying in the scalp, but the 2026 study found it in the blood after a single scalp application.
